title: ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्यमा अलङ्कारविधान 'Dalbahadur' Khandakavyama Alankarbidhan
nepali: ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्यका खण्डकाव्यकार कृष्णप्रसाद वस्ती हुन् । उनको ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्य र सो काव्यमा विधान गरिएका प्रमुख अलङ्कारहरूलाई चिनाउने उद्देश्यका साथ तयार पारिएको प्रस्तुत लेखकोशीर्षक ‘वस्ती गुरुको ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्यमा अलङ्कारविधान हो’ । वस्ती गुरुको जीवनी व्यक्तित्व, कृतित्व तथा पूर्वीय समालोचना पद्धतिको एक प्रमुख सम्प्रदाय अलङ्कारवाद अनुरूप ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्यमा के कस्ता अलङ्कारहरूको विधान गरिएको छ । त्यसका लागि अध्ययन गरिएका सामग्रीहरूमा उनकै स्मृतिमा प्रकाशित स्मृतिग्रन्थ र त्यही ग्रन्थमा समेटिएको ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्य र त्यसको पृष्ठभूमि, लेखहरू, समालोचनात्मक पुस्तक, शब्दकोशादि प्रमुख हुन् । यस लेखमा खण्डकाव्यकारको सङ्क्षिप्त जीवनी, कृतिको विवरण, ‘दलबहादुर’ खण्डकाव्यको कथावस्तु, वशेषता र अलङ्कारको परिचय सहित यस काव्यमा विधान गरिएका १९ ओटा अलङ्कारको सलक्षण विश्लेषणत्मक अध्ययन गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनबाट पूर्वीय काव्यशास्त्र अन्तर्गतको अलङ्कार सिद्धान्तको प्रयोगात्मक पक्षलाई नेपाली भाषामा कविता रचना गर्ने कविहरूले कसरी त्यसको विधान गर्दारहेछन् भन्ने अध्ययन गर्न खोजिएको छ । यसरी हेर्दा कविहरूले अलङ्कार प्रस्तुतिकै लागि कविताकाव्यको रचना गर्दा रहेछन् कि कविताकाव्य रचना गर्दै जाँदा अलङ्कारको आयोजना स्वतःस्पूmर्त रूपमा हुँदै जाँदोरहेछ भन्ने कुरा हेरिएको छ । यसरी हेर्दा कवि वस्ती आलङ्कार प्रस्तुतिका लागि कविता लेख्ने कवि होइन रहेछन् । बरु उनले कविताकाव्य रचना गर्दैजाँदा अलङ्कारहरूको विधान स्वतः हुँदै जाँदो रहेछ भन्ने कुरा देखिएको छ ।
american_english: The khandakavya poet of 'Dalbahadur' is Krishnaprasad Wasti. This article, prepared with the aim of introducing his 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya and the principal figures of speech (alankara) deployed in that poem, is titled 'Alankarbidhan in Wasti Guru's Dalbahadur Khandakavya.' In line with Wasti Guru's life story, personality and works, and with Alankarvada, one of the major schools of the Eastern critical tradition, it examines which figures of speech have been deployed in the 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya. For this purpose, the main materials studied are the smriti (commemorative) granth published in his memory, the 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya included in that same granth along with its background, articles, critical books, dictionaries and the like. The article contains a brief biography of the khandakavya poet, a description of the work, an introduction to the plot, the special features and the alankar, together with an analytic study of the characteristics of the 19 alankar deployed in this poem. Through this study, an attempt has been made to examine how poets composing poems in Nepali employ the practical aspect of alankar theory within Eastern poetics. In this way, it is seen whether poets compose poetic works merely for the sake of presenting alankar, or whether the arrangement of alankar proceeds of its own accord, spontaneously, as the poetic works are composed. Seen in this way, poet Wasti turns out not to be a poet who writes poetry for the sake of presenting alankar. Rather, it has been seen that as he went on composing poetic works, the deployment of alankar happened of its own accord.
british_english: The poet of the 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya is Krishnaprasad Wasti. The present article, prepared with a view to acquainting readers with his 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya and the principal rhetorical figures (alankara) deployed in it, is entitled 'Alankarvidhan in Wasti Guru's Dalbahadur Khandakavya.' In keeping with Wasti Guru's life, personality and oeuvre, and with Alankarvada, a major school of the Eastern critical tradition, the article considers which figures of speech have been deployed in the 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya. For this purpose, the principal materials studied are the commemorative volume (smriti granth) published in his memory, the 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya incorporated in that very volume, along with its background, articles, critical books, dictionaries and the like. The article presents a concise biography of the poet of the khandakavya, an account of the work, an introduction to the plot, the noteworthy characteristics and the alankara, and an analytic study of the characteristic features of the 19 alankara deployed in this poem. By means of this study, an attempt has been made to examine how poets composing in Nepali put the practical side of the theory of alankara within Eastern poetics into practice. Viewed thus, it is observed whether poets compose poetic works merely for the sake of presenting alankara, or whether the arrangement of alankara advances spontaneously of itself as the poetic works take shape. So viewed, the poet Wasti proves not to be a poet who writes poetry in order to present alankara. Rather, it has been observed that, as he composed his poetic works, the deployment of alankara proceeded of itself.

In line with Wasti Guru's life, personality and body of work, and with Alankarvada, a major school of Eastern critical thought, it looks at which alankara have been used in the 'Dalbahadur' khandakavya. Looked at this way, poet Wasti turns out not to be a poet who writes poems for the sake of showing off alankara. Rather, it seems that as he composed poetic works, the deployment of alankara took place of its own accord.
